LanguageData.CC_Settings_LandRecovers_Tip: Ground a fire burned, a wood the colony felled, and trees or grass a sickness killed come back in stages over the growing days (days that average 6 °C or more): grass after 2, brush after 12, young trees of the kind that stood there after 25, and woods after 60, where wood stood. The land's own wild plants are set on the bare ground of it a few a day; nothing in the home area, a zone, on a floor, under a roof or next to a building. A felled wood let grow back is told to the Mossborn. Where the colony's animals crowd a pasture and the grass can't keep up for six days, a few bare cells a day wear to packed earth (rich soil thins to soil, marshy ground churns to mud), a quarter of the good ground at most; rested twenty growing days, it comes back as it was. Burns and fellings are noted through the deeper game hooks.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_LandRecovers: Burnt and felled ground grows back in stages; overgrazed pastures wear bare and recover when rested.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_LandSickness_Tip: Now and then, about once in ninety growing days and three times as often while the region has a blight, a sickness gets into the wild plants of a home map: a wilt that goes from tree to tree among trees of one kind, a rust that kills patches of grass (and some wild grazers move off), or a rot in the wild berry bushes. Sick plants wear the game's blighted look, and a wilting tree stands bare. It spreads to its kind nearby each growing day, more after rain for the rust and the rot, and not in the cold; a sick plant dies after some days (a tree ten, a grass five, a bush seven). It ends when nothing sick is left, after 45 days, or after three cold days. The council is asked whether to cut it out, burn it out at the far edge on a dry day, or let it run. Needs the deeper game hooks.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_LandSickness: A wilt, a rust or a rot now and then in the wild plants, and the council asked what to do.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_LandWater_Tip: Still water (shallow water and marsh, never deep water, rivers, the sea or hot springs) follows the season. After four days of a dry spell its edge turns to mud, and the outer mud to soil, up to three cells in from the old edge. After four days of a wet spell the open ground beside it turns to mud, the ring next to the water then to marsh, up to two cells out, never into the home area, a zone, a floor or within two cells of a building. What one spell left goes back to the map's own edge first when the other comes, and slowly when the season is as usual. Fish follow: a shrunk pond holds no more fish than it can, a filled one gains a few. Switched off, the water goes back to its own edge.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_LandWater: Ponds and marsh edges dry to mud in a drought and swell in wet weather, then go back.
